title: Randomization & Constraint - Sum equals to 9
description: Randomize two integers so that their sum is exactly 9 and both values stay positive.
requirements: Implement the constraint block in class Sum9 so randomize() always produces a > 0, b > 0 and a + b == 9.
hint: Use a single constraint block with three expressions: a > 0, b > 0, and a + b == 9.

examples.explanation: Every randomization must satisfy the sum.

test_cases.expected: a + b == 9 and a > 0 and b > 0

title: Shallow Copy
description: Create a shallow copy of a Packet object. The copy must share the Payload handle with the original object.
requirements: Implement Packet::copy(). Return a new Packet whose addr is copied and whose payload handle points at the same Payload object.
hint: A shallow copy copies the class handle. Assign p.payload = payload instead of allocating a new Payload.

examples.explanation: Writing through the copy is visible in the original.

title: Deep Copy
description: Create a deep copy of a Packet object. The copy must own an independent Payload object.
requirements: Implement Packet::deep_copy(). Copy addr and allocate a new Payload with the same values so the original is not modified through the copy.
hint: Allocate a new Payload and copy each value. Do not assign p.payload = payload.

examples.explanation: Writing through the deep copy leaves the original unchanged.

title: Copy Methods
description: Implement both shallow and deep copy methods on the same class and observe how they differ.
requirements: Implement Record::copy() as a shallow copy and Record::deep_copy() as a deep copy. Record holds a Payload handle.
hint: copy() assigns the payload handle; deep_copy() allocates a new Payload and copies each value.

test_cases.expected: copy shares payload, deep_copy is independent

title: Array in Ascending Order
description: Sort a dynamic array of integers in ascending order in place.
requirements: Implement sort_ascending(ref int arr[]) so the array is sorted from smallest to largest in place.
hint: A simple bubble sort is enough. Compare adjacent elements and swap when the left one is larger.

title: Sliding Window Sum
description: Compute the sum of every contiguous window of size k in an integer array.
requirements: Implement sliding_window_sum(int arr[], int k, ref int out[]). Fill out with arr.size()-k+1 window sums. Return an empty out when k <= 0 or k > arr.size().
hint: Use a nested loop: the outer loop walks the starting index and the inner loop adds k elements.

title: Rearrange an Array
description: Move every zero in an integer array to the end while preserving the order of the non-zero values.
requirements: Implement move_zeros_to_end(ref int arr[]). Non-zero values keep their relative order; all zeros move to the end.
hint: Keep a write index. Copy each non-zero value forward, then fill the remaining positions with zero.

title: No Consecutive 7's
description: Randomize an array of 10 nibbles so that no two adjacent elements are both 7.
requirements: Add a constraint to class No77 that forbids arr[i] == 7 and arr[i-1] == 7 for every i > 0.
hint: Use foreach and guard the comparison with if (i > 0). The forbidden pair is arr[i] == 7 && arr[i-1] == 7.

examples.explanation: The constraint applies to every adjacent pair.

title: Checksum-Consistent Transaction
description: Randomize an 8-byte payload and a checksum that equals the XOR of all payload bytes.
requirements: Add a constraint to class Txn so checksum always equals payload[0] ^ payload[1] ^ ... ^ payload[7].
hint: Wrap the XOR expression in parentheses: checksum == (payload[0] ^ ... ^ payload[7]).

title: Randomization & Constraint - Array Pattern
description: Randomize an array so that it follows the pattern 0, 2, 4, ..., 14.
requirements: Add a constraint to class Pattern so arr[0] == 0 and arr[i] == arr[i-1] + 2 for every i > 0.
hint: Pin arr[0] to 0 and use foreach with if (i > 0) to relate each element to the previous one.

examples.explanation: A deterministic array pattern built by constraints.

title: Reverse an Array
description: Reverse a dynamic array of integers in place.
requirements: Implement reverse_array(ref int arr[]) so the first element becomes last and vice versa.
hint: Swap arr[i] with arr[n-1-i] for i from 0 to n/2 - 1.

title: Find Duplicate Elements in an Array
description: Collect each value that appears more than once in an integer array.
requirements: Implement find_duplicates(int arr[], ref int dups[]). Fill dups with each repeated value exactly once.
hint: Use a queue to remember values already added, then copy the queue into dups at the end.

title: Find First & Second Largest in an Array
description: Return the largest and second-largest distinct values in an integer array.
requirements: Implement first_second_largest(int arr[], ref int first, ref int second). For an array with one distinct value, set both outputs to that value.
hint: Track whether a second distinct value has been seen. Compare against first first, then against second.

title: Array Manipulations
description: Rotate a dynamic array left by k positions.
requirements: Implement rotate_left(ref int arr[], int k). Positive k rotates left; negative k rotates right. k may be larger than the array size.
hint: Normalize k with k % n, then save the first k elements in a temporary array before shifting the rest.

title: Fork-Join 2
description: Use fork...join_any and wait fork so both branches of a task complete before it returns.
requirements: Implement ForkJoin2::run(). Start two branches (#10 sets a=1, #20 sets b=2), use join_any, then wait fork.
hint: join_any returns when the first branch finishes. wait fork then waits for the remaining branch.

title: Fork-Join
description: Use fork...join so a task waits for both parallel branches before returning.
requirements: Implement ForkJoin::run(). Start two branches (#5 sets a=10, #10 sets b=20) and use join.
hint: fork...join blocks until every branch finishes, so both a and b are updated.

title: Safe Memory Region Copy - Memory Operations
description: Copy a byte range between two dynamic arrays with full bounds checking.
requirements: Implement SafeMem::copy_region(). Return 1 and copy len bytes on success. Return 0 for a negative length or any out-of-bounds source/destination range.
hint: Check len, src_start, and dst_start first. Then check src_start + len <= src.size() and dst_start + len <= dst.size().

examples.explanation: Source range would read past the end.

title: Polymorphism
description: Use virtual methods so a base-class handle dispatches to Rectangle and Circle implementations.
requirements: Override area() and name() in Rectangle and Circle. Rectangle area is w*h; Circle area is 3*r*r.
hint: Declare area() and name() as virtual in the derived classes and return the computed values.

test_cases.input: Shape handles to Rectangle(3,4) and Circle(2)

title: Find First Non-Zero Bit Position
description: Return the index of the least-significant set bit in a 32-bit value.
requirements: Implement first_nonzero_bit(bit [31:0] value). Return the bit index (0..31) of the first 1 from the LSB, or -1 when value is zero.
hint: Loop from bit 0 upward and return i as soon as value[i] is 1. Return -1 after the loop.

examples.explanation: Bit 8 is the first set bit.

title: Write a Function That Returns a Result
description: Write an iterative function that returns the nth Fibonacci number.
requirements: Implement fibonacci(int n). Return F(0)=0, F(1)=1, and -1 for negative n.
hint: Keep two previous values and iterate from 1 to n. Handle n < 0 and n == 0 first.

title: Dynamic Array & Queue Operations
description: Maintain a dynamic array and a queue together through add, remove, and sum operations.
requirements: Implement DataStore::add(), remove_first(), and total(). add() appends to both dyn and q; remove_first() removes the first element from both and returns it (or -1 when empty); total() sums dyn.
hint: Use new[size](old) to grow the dynamic array, push_back for the queue, pop_front for removal, and shift the dynamic array left after a pop.

examples.explanation: The front element is removed from both.

title: Count Even Numbers in an Array
description: Count how many values in an integer array are even.
requirements: Implement count_even(int arr[]) and return the number of values where arr[i] % 2 == 0.
hint: Use foreach and increment a counter when arr[i] % 2 == 0. Zero is even.

title: Randomization and Constraints - Multiple of 4
description: Randomize an 8-bit value that is a multiple of 4 and no greater than 100.
requirements: Add a constraint to class Multiple4 so x <= 100 and x[1:0] == 2'b00 (the low two bits are zero).
hint: A multiple of 4 has its two least-significant bits equal to zero. Constrain x[1:0] == 2'b00 and x <= 100.
